walkDown:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production walking-animation sprite layers for an existing 2D game.
Input image 1 is the exact character identity and idle-pose reference. Create FOUR closely matching full-body frames of this SAME girl WALKING DOWN toward the camera, arranged in a square 2-by-2 equal-cell sheet on true transparent alpha. Keep the same hand-painted chibi style, exact face, gray eyes, black cat ears, long black hair, long black dress with ruffled hem, small cross necklace, and chunky black buckle shoes. Keep proportions and all four faces almost identical to the input.
Natural quiet WALK, not marching or hopping. Small alternating heel-to-toe steps beneath the long dress, feet comfortably hip-width apart. Both lower legs/boots must remain readable and distinct, never merged into one centered foot, never crossed or pigeon-toed. Knees stay concealed under the long skirt; only short ankles show. Both toes point toward the viewer. Keep both shoulders facing directly forward and the head upright. Subtle 1–2% body bob, small alternating skirt sway and lagging hair motion. No exaggerated lifted knee, kick, leap or squat.
FOUR EXACT PHASES IN READING ORDER:
top left: her RIGHT foot (screen LEFT) is slightly forward and planted, LEFT foot screen-right slightly behind.
top right: weight passes over the right foot while the left foot comes forward beside it, both boots visible; very small foot lift.
bottom left: her LEFT foot (screen RIGHT) slightly forward and planted, RIGHT foot screen-left slightly behind.
bottom right: opposite passing phase, weight over left foot while right foot comes forward beside it, both boots visible. This leads smoothly back to top-left.
The sword ALWAYS stays in her anatomical RIGHT hand on SCREEN LEFT. One silver longsword, held low diagonally to the BOTTOM LEFT, continuous wrist, closed grip connected to the dark handle. The screen-right left hand stays EMPTY, relaxed with a tiny natural swing. Do not mirror the whole character or switch the sword hand. Keep sword angle, length and hilt consistent across all four frames, do not swing/attack.
Each isolated sprite occupies about 78% of a quadrant's height, centered within its own quadrant, BOTH complete shoes plus the full sword strictly inside with ample clear margins. All frames use the same character scale, head height and planted-foot baseline. No camera/view changes, no text, grid lines, floor shadows, scenery or extra limbs. Preserve transparent alpha, including between the legs and around the sword.
passingCorrection:
Precise animation phase correction to this existing 2x2 transparent walking sprite sheet. KEEP the TOP-LEFT and BOTTOM-LEFT frames completely unchanged: these are good right-foot-forward and left-foot-forward contact frames.
Change ONLY the lower skirt/ankles/shoes of the TOP-RIGHT and BOTTOM-RIGHT frames so they become PASSING poses, not another long front/back step. Keep their upper body, face, ears, hair, scale, position, sword, right-hand grip, grid and transparency unchanged.
TOP-RIGHT: her RIGHT foot on SCREEN LEFT is the supporting planted foot, directly below her right hip. Her LEFT foot on SCREEN RIGHT is moving PAST it; bring both boots close to the SAME vertical depth/height, with the lifted left boot's sole only about 8 pixels HIGHER than the planted right boot's sole (relative to the 640px quadrant shown). Both toes toward viewer, feet next to each other rather than one boot far in front. Keep the lifted foot separate and visible. Do not lift the knee out of the dress. Short ankles only.
BOTTOM-RIGHT: opposite passing phase: her LEFT foot on SCREEN RIGHT planted, right boot on SCREEN LEFT passing beside it, its sole only about 8 pixels HIGHER. Again the two boots are next to each other, at almost the SAME vertical depth, not one long forward step. Both feet distinct, not crossed, two legs, no extra feet.
Use the SAME boots and correct anatomical ankle connections. The dress hem should fall naturally with only slight alternating sway. This completes the loop: right contact, right support/left passing, left contact, left support/right passing. Do NOT mirror the character: the sword stays in the screen-LEFT right hand in all four frames. Preserve true transparent alpha. No background, grid or shadows.
packing: Four complete sprites were separated at the transparent row gap (y=493 after resizing the selected result to 1024px), then packed into equal 512px source cells at one shared scale. Each face centroid is aligned to (280,176) with transparent margins. The build script aligns the final frames by face, uses a shared scale and a one-pixel upward passing-phase bob, and packs a four-frame strip.
